title: Console Spine: Mode-aware Sidebar Compression and Temporal Routing
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: The current console navigation mixes operational workflows (deploy/rollouts), observability (dashboards/traces), and cost controls in a flat left rail. This causes discovery friction for engineers switching contexts (debugging vs cost analysis vs canary rollouts), increases accidental navigation, and hides critical signals during incidents. Objective: Prototype and validate a ‘mode-aware’ console spine that compresses and reorients the sidebar based on current user intent (Observability, Deploy, Billing, Admin), surface lightweight temporal routing for fast context switching (time-travel to prior workspace state), and give quick access to rollout controls and cost lenses without breaking existing keyboard flows.
background: This work builds on Console Navigation Redesign themes and complements ENG’s routing flags for per-route metadata. Prior design explorations focused on hub-and-spoke and compact rails; this ticket tests a hybrid approach: compressive spine + micro-hubs that expose contextual cost/rollout cards. We must preserve keyboard accessibility and deep-linking semantics (URL + route-state), and keep parity with Dedicated/Private console capabilities.
goals: Reduce average time-to-task when switching between operational modes by 25% in prototype lab tests
Expose token-level cost lens adjacent to relevant dashboards and routes
Provide persistent rollout controls (canary toggle, traffic split) in a minimal header when in Deploy mode
Support temporal routing so users can pivot console state to a selected time window without losing filters
out_of_scope: Full redesign of billing pages (will be follow-up PM work)
Replacing existing rollout backend—this is a UI/flow layer that talks to current rollout APIs
Mobile-first rework (mobile surfaces will be handled in separate ticket)
constraints: Must not require server-side schema changes for deep links; prefer route-state encoding and query params
Left rail width must remain within 56px compressed and 280px expanded to accommodate current breakpoint grid
Keyboard-only users must be able to switch modes and access cost lenses in <= 3 keystrokes
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Progressive disclosure vs everything-on-rail: chose progressive disclosure (compressive spine + micro-hub panels) to reduce visual noise while keeping features one click away
Contextual rollouts in header vs a full-screen modal: header makes quick adjustments faster but limits complex tooling; complex rollout configuration will remain in full page
Temporal routing will be implemented client-side using cached filter snapshots to avoid backend migrations; this increases client memory usage but speeds prototyping
acceptance_criteria: Mode-aware spine toggles between Observability/Deploy/Billing/Admin and exposes mode-specific micro-hub when selected
Temporal routing control opens a time selector and applies filters without page reload; URL encodes the time-slice for sharing
Cost lens displays token breakdown for the active route and links to full cost dashboard
Rollout mini-controls allow canary on/off and a traffic split slider; actions map to existing rollout API (ENG-6003) and show success/failure toast
Keyboard navigation test script passes: mode switch, micro-hub open, cost lens focus within 3 keystrokes
engineering_tasks: ENG-5921: Add route metadata hook to expose 'mode' hint to client
ENG-6003: Implement minimal rollout API endpoint for quick toggle (integration only; full rollout remains unchanged)
ENG-6075: Client-side snapshot store for temporal routing (local/session storage)
design_notes: Design uses a single persistent spine component that swaps micro-hub contents based on mode. Micro-hubs are small panels (max 420px) layered over main canvas to avoid route churn.
Visual language aligns with current console tokens but introduces 'mode color accents' to quickly communicate intent (Observability = teal, Deploy = amber, Billing = indigo, Admin = slate).
We use subtle motion to indicate compression/expansion; motion timings calibrated to 120–180ms for perceived snappiness.
usability_testing_plan: Recruit 8 engineers across infra and app teams (mix of Hosted/Dedicated users)
Tasks: (1) find cost of model X over last 30 days, (2) enable canary for route Y with 10% traffic, (3) switch console to a prior workspace snapshot
Metrics: task completion time, errors, subjective satisfaction (SUS), and open feedback
Success criterion: mean task time reduction >= 25% versus baseline prototypes
risks: If ENG routing metadata is delayed, the spine will revert to a heuristic mode detection which may mismatch user intent
Temporal snapshots may grow large for heavy dashboards; may require pruning or server-side snapshots in a follow-up
Cost lens accuracy depends on aggregated token counters from the telemetry pipeline (coordination with Observability required)
Accessibility regressions if keyboard focus is not carefully managed when micro-hubs appear
